sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Grave Gloveworts** are a type of bolstering material in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree. They are used to upgrade the power of Spirit Ashes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Grave Gloveworts are the standard form of the white glovewort found growing in the many catacombs of the Lands Between. After Roderika becomes a spirit tuner at the Roundtable Hold, she can use Grave Gloveworts to incrementally upgrade the power and durability of Ashes up to a maximum of **+10**.

sections.heading: List of Grave Gloveworts
sections.markdown: There are **10** varieties of Grave Gloveworts to be found in the game.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Grave Gloveworts may be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold after turning in Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearings:
 - [[item:glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-1|Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [1]]] unlocks the sale of Grave Gloveworts 1, 2, and 3.
 - [[item:glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-2|Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [2]]] unlocks the sale of Grave Gloveworts 4, 5, and 6.
 - [[item:glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-3|Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [3]]] unlocks the sale of Grave Gloveworts 7, 8, and 9.
- Great Grave Gloveworts are used to upgrade standard Spirit Ashes to +10, but only a limited number can be obtained per playthrough. A total of **6** can be found in the base game, with an additional **6** located in the Realm of Shadow, bringing the total to **12** per playthrough.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: This page lists a number of glitches and bugs that have been recorded throughout Elden Ring's history.

sections.heading: Two-Minute Disconnect
sections.markdown:
The biggest issue that has been plaguing the multiplayer on the PC platform is the awfully frequent “two-minute disconnections”. Consoles don’t have this issue, so players have been left to believe it has to do with the “Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC)” software that was added to *Elden Ring*. Two minutes after establishing a multiplayer connection, players appear to be disconnected for failing to be validated by Easy Anti-Cheat’s services. However, this is obviously not working correctly as it happens at random for everyone who’s playing the game, the only consistent factor is that it happens at the two-minute mark.

The video goes into further technical detail.

sections.heading: Input Drops
sections.markdown: There are various animation interactions within *Elden Ring* which have been found to have clearly unintended behavior, such as consistently not taking player inputs at points which are intended. This results in combat feeling clunky and unfair, as players doubt and question if the game is even responding to their inputs when it’s supposed to. These are similar to exploits and passive glitches, which tend to affect the game as a whole negatively for all players, but in a way that is difficult for most to pin down. The following are input drop issues that players have been able to identify:

sections.heading: Block-Sprint Input Drop
sections.markdown:
When stopping a sprint and lowering your guard around the same time, any action the player inputs will be dropped (e.g. rolling, attacking).
 ► 0:29 ­ ­ ­ Block-sprint input drop
­

sections.heading: Two-Hand-Jumping-Input-Drop
sections.markdown:
When continuing to sprint after a jump, the player cannot queue a light attack action for a significant amount of time after landing, while any other input works including guarding. This does not occur when 1-handing weapons.
At the below timestamp, you can see the keyboard “Light Attack” input being repeatedly dropped, only while 2-handing and after landing from a sprinting jump.
 ► 2:38 ­ ­ ­ Two-hand jumping input drop
­

sections.heading: Damage Occurrence Input Drop
sections.markdown: When the player receives damage that does not stun them, certain actions seem to be cleared from the input queue such as roll dodging, which causes players to be hit again as they expected the game to not clear their input. This has been confirmed to be a result of the damage occurrence and not any misconceptions with queue timing.

sections.heading: Moving Toggle Input Drop
sections.markdown:
While moving during a toggle (weapon swap/2-handing) animation, it is impossible to buffer another action out of the animation until it finishes. Despite this, you are still able to buffer actions when toggling while standing still.
At the timestamp below, you can see the keyboard “Heavy Attack” input being dropped only while doing a moving toggle.
 ► 1:59 ­ ­ ­ Moving toggle input drop

 Explanation video by Amir

sections.heading: Aim Punch
sections.markdown:
When a character in the middle of an attack animation is hit by an attack and is not interrupted out of it (either due to poise, or the attack not having any hitstun), the character still animates a bit in reaction to the damage. This animation is so strong, that it can frequently cause attacks to miss even if they would have certainly hit normally.

- At the below timestamp for example. The weapon would have hit the enemy directly in front of the player normally, but due to aim punch, the swing is redirected to the left and misses. Some of these examples in this video are so silly, that the weapon can even be seen swinging 360 degrees on a random axis.
- The same video at the following timestamp suggests a good solution for this issue implemented in one of Elden Ring’s predecessors.

sections.heading: Perpetual Casting
sections.markdown:
By generating an absurd amount of bullets, players can glitch their character to fire them off indefinitely.
The following video showcases this exploit and explains its mechanics and cause in detail:

sections.heading: Crouch Run Stamina Exploit
sections.markdown:
Entering or exiting crouch while running does not restrict stamina regeneration, nor consume stamina during those animations. This is clearly unintentional, as the regular running animation does consume stamina. The consequence of this glitch is that it allows players to continue running while in combat without breaks for stamina regeneration, as they lose minimal speed from entering and exiting crouch.

The following video showcases and explains additional details on the impact of this exploit:

sections.heading: Blessed Dew Talisman Regen Glitch
sections.markdown:
Rapidly equipping and unequipping the Blessed Dew Talisman allows the user to restore HP far faster than intended.

The following video showcases this glitch:

sections.heading: Infinite Health Helmet Swap Glitch
sections.markdown: By swapping between the Karolos Glintstone Crown and some other Glintstone Crowns, players can restore their entire health bar in a matter of seconds at no cost. This allows players to regenerate hundreds of health points per second, due to an issue with the status and attribute altering effects of the crowns.

sections.heading: Glitched Chain Casting
sections.markdown:
We are not certain how much of chaining casts between spells is intentional, but there are certain chain cast interactions that are clearly not intended. When queuing a spell out of a different spell that can chain cast such as Bestial Sling, it may attempt to play the third cast animation of the queued spell. However, not all spells that have the ability to chain cast also have a third casting animation. If the spell is prompted to play the third casting animation and does not have one, it appears to default to the Glintstone Pebble spell’s third cast animation. This causes many strange interactions.

- This video showcases the difference between possibly intentional inter-spell chain casting and clearly unintentionally glitched casting:
Update: As of patch 1.05, several forms of chain casting including ones that play a clearly incorrect animation have been patched out. However, there are still methods of chain casting in the game. Cross-spell chain casting can still be achieved by queuing the spell out of a jump cast of another spell. Additionally, spells that utilize the same animation set can chain cast between each other as they would with themselves.*

sections.heading: Bolus Swap
sections.markdown:
Similar to the patched sprint pivot swap glitch, this glitch allows you to use a weapon skill on any other weapon, by way of a very tightly timed inventory unequip at the end of a quick consumable animation (such as Preserving Boluses). The capabilities of this glitch include putting any skill buffs on weapons that cannot be buffed using spells or consumables, or the use of weapon skills on unintended armaments such as the Bloodboon Ritual skill on Vyke’s War Spear.

The steps to execute this glitch are as follows:
- 1. Equip the armament with the skill you wish to use in your off-hand.
- 2. Equip the armament that you want to transfer the skill animation to in your right hand.
- 3. Two-hand the armament in your off-hand.
- 4. Use a quick eating consumable such as a Preserving Bolus.
- 5. Queue the skill use action (L2 on a PlayStation Controller).
- 6. Near the end of the animation, enter your inventory and press the unequip button on your left hand armament slot, removing the weapon you currently have two-handed.
- 7. If timed correctly, your character should be doing the skill of the armament you just removed.
Here is a video showcasing the glitch and how to execute it:

sections.heading: Off-Hand Stance Swap
sections.markdown: This bug allows the player to use weapon skills with a glitched lower-body state, which allows them to walk or run during skills that would normally prevent player-controlled movement.

sections.markdown: Great Jar** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He offers a trial that, if completed, rewards the player with the Great-Jar's Arsenal talisman.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Great-Jar is located in front of a Colosseum structure at Caelid, but can only be accessed late in the game from an elevator located in Siofra River.

After speaking to it for the first time, three red summon signs will appear nearby, each allowing to summon a Knight of the Great Jar. After defeating all three summons without dying, the player will be rewarded.

sections.heading: Knights of the Great Jar
sections.markdown:
The Knights of the Great Jar are copies of other players who have already completed the challenge. In case of playing offline, the game provides three default options:

One wields a Magic affinity Estoc and an Albinauric Staff with which it casts Carian Phalanx and Magic Glintblade, and wears the Marionette Soldier Birdhelm, Lusat's Robe, and unknown hand and leg piece.

Another wields a Miséricorde with the Poison Moth Flight skill and a Buckler to parry with, and wears the Prophet Blindfold, Raptor's Black Feathers, an unknown hand piece, and Leather Boots.

The third combatant wields a Great Mace with the Prayerful Strike skill and a Banished Knight's Shield, and wears the Banished Knight Helm, Ronin's Armor, an unknown hand piece, and Raging Wolf Greaves.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Haligtree Soldiers are frontline infantrymen loyal to Miquella the Kind, one of the Demigods who participated in the Shattering. They support the Haligtree Knights and Haligtree Foot Soldiers in continued defense of the rotting Haligtree, despite their Empyrean's absence.

A braided crown of unalloyed gold adorns their helmets. They wear bloodstained, rusted iron armor beneath a white surcoat depicting the Haligtree, a symbol of Miquella. In this rendition, fresh buds emerge from a Haligtree sapling supported by a trellis.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Golden Lineage** is a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The Golden Lineage is the royal bloodline descended from the union of Lord Godfrey and Queen Marika. A two-headed war axe and a golden lion serves as the emblem of their family, the former representing the favorite weapon of their founding patriarch and the latter being the likeness of his loyal advisor Serosh, Lord of Beasts.

sections.heading: **Founders**
sections.markdown:
After their victory against the giants and the Sealing of Destined Death, the fate of the Erdtree and the Golden Order was considered secured and thus the Elden Lord, Godfrey and God-Queen, Marika established a royal lineage with their first demigod children together, with Beast Regent, Serosh and his counseling serving as a guide for the generations to come.

Before long, Godfrey continued on his campaign to expand the Golden Order's influence and rule and strengthening his reputation as the Lord of the Battlefield, a reputation that would be quickly followed up in modest by their immediate children, but became a suffocating shadow that would progressively tower higher and higher over his later descendants.

sections.heading: **First Descendants**
sections.markdown:
The immediate descendants of their family's founders, these children would be the first to carry the unified blood of both Godfrey and Marika.

Many of these individuals would go on to make their names known, forging their own stories and pursue their own goals, fueled by their own convictions. Indeed these apples did truly not fall far from their tree.

sections.heading: **Later Descendants**
sections.markdown:
Unlike the first generation after Godfrey, many of the later descendants would become obsessed with their pedigree and status as a reputable, important bloodline. Continuously riding the glory of their founding father's accomplishments while progressively becoming less and less comparable to his greatness with each passing generation.

The current-day dregs of the golden lineage would go desperately searching for power and purpose in the past. Excavating for ancient relics and surrounding themselves with artifacts of a golden era, an era they played no part in and had long since passed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Before the Tarnished battles him, Godrick refers to a fallen dragon as "trueborn heir" and a "kindred". While it's unlikely that he is actually related to the dragon by blood, he is likely evoking the fraternal relationship established between Godwyn the Golden and Ancient Dragon Fortissax, and thus the Golden Lineage and dragonkind. They are also related on a thematic level, as the specific species of dragon Godrick is speaking to is in a similar existential situation as he is, a lesser descendant of greater ancestors. Even in the moment where he grafts the dragon's head onto himself, Godrick continues to reafirm the dragon's value, reffering to it as "the truest of dragons". As by reafirming it's value, he is by extention attempting to affirm his own value as well.
- Cut content suggests that Gatekeeper Gostoc is actually a son of Godrick the Grafted. Should this still be true in the final game, then this would make Gostoc a member of the Golden Lineage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Golems** are a type of autonomous constructs found throughout the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Typically made of stone by ancient civilizations now gone to ruin, golems are generally resistant to all common status ailments. Today, they are frequently positioned as guards of tombs and other sacred sites.

Long ago, it is said that a golem crafter employed a crystal tool that heavily resembles what would become the chiseled Crystal Darts that can be crafted and discovered across the world today. If enough of these darts penetrate a single golem in quick enough succession, that golem will malfunction and begin indiscriminately attacking everything in its vicinity (including its own allies) for a short period of time. This applies only to imps, Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, Guardian Golems, and Golem Smiths Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.markdown: Haligtree Knights** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Knights who have vowed to serve Miquella's Haligtree, they carry metal greatshields depicting the Haligtree with unalloyed gold, possessing high holy damage negation. Their armor is of such quality that time has yet to dull their luster; their left breast is emblazoned with the crest of the Haligtree, and they wear helms graced with crowns of unalloyed gold that increase faith. They also carry a flower signifying faith in the Haligtree, thought to be beloved by the Empyrean Miquella in his youth.

Haligtree Knights are strong and skilled warriors. Largely armed with greatswords, some also wield a shield while others switch to a greatbow for powerful long-ranged attacks. A select few carry Partisan spears instead of a sword. No matter their armament, these knights are blessed with access to a number of magical skills that can aid them in battle, such as Glintstone Pebble and Sacred Order, the latter of which allows them to regenerate health. Curiously, they even possess a Flask of Wondrous Physick which fully heals them when consumed.

Glintstone** are a family of Sorceries in Elden Ring. The practice of this type of magic is said to have begun with an Ancient Astrologer's discovery of the Primeval Current and since then has served as a main focus of study amongst many sorcerers.

The Academy of Raya Lucaria in particular was founded with the sole purpose of studying this form of magic and thus many of the spells of this category find their origins at the academy, their varitiy of complexities making for excellent material of study for sorceres at different skill levels. Glintstone has become so integral to the sorcerous arts that many of its spells have become elementary knowledge among spell casters of all kinds.

All glintstone sorceries deal pure Magic Damage and have Intelligence requirements.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Gravity Sorceries** are a school of magic in Elden Ring. The power of gravity is frequently seen used by beings from beyond the stars. The knowledge of these arts were introduced to mankind by the enigmatic Alabaster Lords and Onyx Lords.

Gravity sorceries either deal pure Magic Damage or a mixture of Physical and Magic damage and have Intelligence requirements. They are known for their ability to either forcibly pull targets closer to oneself or inflict heavy Stance damage against enemies.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Godskin Apostles were servants of Destined Death, and the followers of the Gloam-Eyed Queen, an Empyrean who cradled them from infancy. They wore hoods and robes stitched together from patches of smooth, pale skin and wielded the god-slaying power of the blackflame, and assimilated inhuman physiology, such as the ability to stretch like Gelmir Man-Serpents, not unlike the Crucible. Though they stand in opposition to the Erdtree, they have golden eyes. Additionally, the faces on their clothes bear the Grace of Gold in their eyes.

The Godskin Nobles were the first of these god-killers, who claimed Noble Presence during their god hunt. Their crusade came to an end when the Gloam-Eyed Queen was defeated by Maliketh, the shadowbound beast of Marika. With the Rune of Death sealed away by Maliketh within his Black Blade, the true power of the Godslayer Incantations was lost.

All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to this percentage-based damage, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.markdown: Gods** are among the most powerful characters in the world of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Queen Marika the Eternal
sections.markdown: Queen Marika the Eternal is the divine sovereign of the Lands Between. She was a Numen woman hailing from a Shaman Village in the Hinterland. As an Empyrean, Marika traveled to the Gate of Divinity atop Enir-Ilim where she ascended to godhood and became the vessel of the Elden Ring. Marika is further known as the mother or step-mother of the demigods, grower of the Erdtree, founder of the Golden Order, slayer of the Fell God as well as the spouse of the Elden Lords Godfrey and Radagon. Although she vanished after the Shattering, Marika influences the Tarnished and her chosen through the golden Guidance of Grace.

sections.heading: Miquella the Kind
sections.markdown: After Godfrey was Tarnished, the demigod Miquella the Kind was born to Queen Marika and Lord Radagon. Despite his eternal youth, he was selected as an Empyrean like his twin sister, Malenia. He was the master inventer of Unalloyed Gold, the grower of the sacred Haligtree, and a coercive charmer. After divesting himself of his flesh, his eye, his fears, his vacillation, and St. Trina—his love and fate—Miquella, like Marika, ascended to godhood at the Gate of Divinity. He used the body of Mohg to resurrect his promised consort, Radahn, in a failed attempt to succeed his mother as sovereign and usher in an Age of Compassion.

sections.heading: Malenia, Goddess of Rot
sections.markdown: Malenia, the undefeated Blade and twin sister of Miquella the Kind, was born afflicted with baleful Scarlet Rot. However, she managed to suppress it with the help of the Blind Swordsman and Miquella's Unalloyed Gold Needle. During her legendary duel with Radahn at the end of the Shattering, she reluctantly unleashed the Scarlet Aeonia. Following this bloom, the Swamp of Aeonia manifested in Caelid, producing the Kindred of Rot. If the Empyrean Malenia is confronted and defeated at the Haligtree, she will blossom for a second time. Her third and final bloom is prophesied to complete her transformation into a true Goddess of Rot. Unlike her twin, Malenia has no interest in establishing her own Order.

sections.heading: Fell God
sections.markdown: The red-haired, one-eyed Fell God of fire is an ancient deity worshipped by the Fire Giants. It is regarded as an malevolent entity that opposes and threatens the Erdtree and the Golden Order. Queen Marika allegedly slew the Fell God during the War Against the Giants, and cursed the last survivor of their race to eternally tend the Flame.. However, the Fell God's still lingers within the giants.

sections.heading: Ancient Dragon God
sections.markdown: Dragonlord Placidusax waited for his fled god to return.

sections.heading: Old Gods
sections.markdown: The old gods ((古い神々, *Furui Kamigami*) were colossal giants who wielded ancient meteoric ore that contained explosive white light. An excavated shard of one of their arrowheads was the treasure of a ruined forge that came after them.

sections.heading: Radiant Gods
sections.markdown: Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow worshipped radiant gods (光を放つ神々, *Hikariohanatsu Kamigami*, lit. Light-Emitting Gods) cloaked in the roar of thunder. It is possible that they are one and the same with the Old Gods, as both are referred to as *kamigami* in the Japanese script, both produce light (their radiance is written with the same kanji as the Old Gods white light, 光), and the legends of them concealing themselves in thunder are reminscent of the thunderstone folklore which provided the real-world inspiration for the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword.

sections.heading: Serpent-God
sections.markdown: The ancient inhabitants of Mt. Gelmir made sacrifices in the name of a Serpent-God. It is likely connected to one of the god-like snakes, such as the Abyssal Serpent and God-Devouring Serpent.

sections.heading: Demigods
sections.markdown: Demigods are powerful beings with the divine blood or power but without possessing true godhood. In the Lands Between most demigods are children or step-children of Queen Marika and the Elden Lords. After Marika shattered the Elden Ring, many demigods acquired Great Runes and became Shardbearers. The Tarnished are guided by Grace to challenge the demigods and claim their Great Runes.

sections.heading: Empyreans
sections.markdown: Empyreans are beings capable of becoming gods. During the Age of the Erdtree, Empyreans were chosen by the Two Fingers. Examples of Empyreans are Marika, Miquella, Ranni, Malenia and the Gloam-Eyed Queen.

sections.heading: Greater Will
sections.markdown: The Greater Will is a mysterious entity or force known for fracturing the One Great, thus creating life and souls in the Lands Between. It once sent the Elden Beast to the Lands Between, which would eventually become the Elden Ring itself. The Greater Will also had other vassals like Metyr and her children, the Two Fingers, who selected Empyreans to become gods. The Greater Will is speculated to have imprisoned Queen Marika after she shattered the Elden Ring. Due to the Greater Will's power to rupture the One Great, create and imprison gods, it can effectively be seen as the supreme being of the *Elden Ring* universe.

sections.heading: Outer Gods
sections.markdown: Outer Gods are extremely powerful entities that exist outside of the Lands Between, the current Order of the Elden Ring or on an higher plane. Examples of outer gods are the Formless Mother, the God of Rot, the Twinbird's God, and the Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Tutelary Deities
sections.markdown:
A tutelary deity is a god or spirit regarded as the guardian, patron, or protector of a specific location, natural feature, individual, lineage, nation, cultural group, or profession. The term "tutelary" derives from roots associated with safety and thus of guardianship.

Hornsent aspired to ascend as tutelary deities by engaging in severe ascetic training. Some became Curseblades or Divine Beast Warriors. Withered corpses of successful tutelary deities, enshrined across the Realm of Shadow, quietly gather Revered Spirit Ash in their palms.

sections.heading: Nox Gods
sections.markdown: The Nox once revered mummified giants seated upon Chair-Crypt thrones, often honored them with Great Ghost Glovewort and other treasures.

sections.heading: Rauh
sections.markdown: The Ancient Ruins of Rauh feature large statues of a woman wearing an octagonal hat. She is associated with the Verdigris Discus and Bondstone. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to the "Rauh goddess" figure. The Golden Crucible originated in Rauh.

sections.markdown: The Grandmother** (大母, *Taibo*) was an unseen character in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Grandmother is a petrified maiden encased within the trunk of a large tree at the Shaman Village in the Hinterland of Scaduview. Roots or branches extend from her body, forming the tree itself. She kneels barefoot, arms outstretched, palms up in open embrace. A dark dress clings to her stone frame, and her eyes are veiled by long silver hair tied in two braids.

She was revered by the oppressed shamans, supposed denizens of another world. After rising to power, Queen Marika severed a braid of her golden hair and left it as an offering to the matriarch of her people. She blessed the village with golden light and left—never to return.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- While her Japanese name, 大母, is rarely used to refer to the mother of ones parents, it can be more literally read as "Great Mother;" the same term is used to refer to Greyoll.
- Her features strongly resemble those of the tortured Jar Dwellers found in Bonny Gaol and elsewhere.
- The headless statue found outside Bonny Village resembles the Grandmother.
- The Grandmother may have embedded herself into the tree to water it with her blood in the way Miquella did his Haligtree.
- The Grandmother may have been a Numen.
- Fractured Marika is found in a statuesque form at the Stone Platform within the Erdtree.
- Her eyes are obscured, which implies blindness.
 - One of her eyes is open while the other is closed, though this cannot be seen under normal gameplay.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Greattree** is an unseen location in Elden Ring. It is mentioned only in a few item descriptions.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The vast network of Greattree roots spreads throughout the Lands Between. The various catacombs and hero's graves of the region were built specifically around these roots. The Greattree roots begin where those of the Erdtree end: the Deeproot Depths—the source of the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers. The two root systems were once connected, which enabled Erdtree Burial.

After Godwyn the Golden received Erdtree Burial at the base of the Erdtree's roots, his soulless body transformed into the Prince of Death. Over time, fragments of the Rune of Death leaked from his body and spread through the roots of the Greattree, giving rise to Deathroot and, ultimately, Those Who Live in Death. Sometime after the Shattering, the two root systems ended up disconnected through the Deathroot corruption, impeding the Erdtree ability to recover bodies and souls through Erdtree Burial.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The roots of the Greattree secrete a special Root Resin used for making various greases.
- Elden Stars, the most ancient of all Erdtree Incantations, is placed near the Great Waterfall Basin Site of Grace at the Deeproot Depths.
 - The Elden Beast's tail resembles golden roots.

- Oak leaves litter the area around the large hollowed-out tree protected by Crucible Knight Siluria.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Several references to the Greattree were not present in the English version 1.00 of Elden Ring. The relevant items instead used placeholder descriptions until a subsequent update.
- The "Greattree roots" are referred to as 大樹根 (*taijune*) in the Japanese version of *Elden Ring*. The term can be translated literally as "big/great tree roots", "great treeroots", or "Great Roots".
- The Japanese version of *Elden Ring* does not appear to use a distinct proper noun corresponding to "Greattree". Instead, it uses the descriptive term *taijune* ("great tree roots"). Compound names such as *Erdtree* and *lampwood* follow a naming convention often associated with literature (e.g., **) and modern fantasy works inspired by it.
- The Finger Reader Crone in the Capital Outskirts refers to the Erdtree as a great tree in her dialogue; "Surely you see it, too? The gold that enshrouds the heavens. The great tree which begets the pillars of light. O Tarnished, hasten to the foot of the tree. And whatever you might face... The Fingers will surely guide you...". The Erdtree is also referred to as a great tree various more times in the Japanese text, such as with the name of the Tree-and-Beast Surcoat. 大樹と獣のサーコート translating to Great Tree and Beast Surcoat.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **God Hunt** was an event mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The god hunt was a campaign launched by the Gloam-Eyed Queen to bring death to the gods of her time. It ended with her defeat and the sealing of the Rune of Death and thus the true power of the Godslayer Incantations.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Rune of Death, also known as Destined Death, was once part of the Elden Ring until it was removed by Queen Marika to give shape to her Golden Order.

The Gloam-Eyed Queen was an Empyrean chosen by her own Two Fingers, and individual with the potential to succeed Marika as vessel of the Elden Ring. At some point between the War Against the Giants, after the order Fire Monks was established to watch over the Flame of Ruin and the end of the Age of Plenty, when the Erdtree's blessed sap was still abundant she managed to get her hands on the Rune of Death, wielding it to empower the black flame she channeled from her spiral greatsword

sections.heading: Battles
sections.markdown:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen raised her Apostles, childrens with serpentine tails that had assimilated inhuman physiology like the Crucible that had created the Erdtree and cradled the newborns in swaddling cloths made of skin. The Queen taught them incantations of the black flame and they used Godslayer's Seals made with obsidian and representing the manipulation of her power.. She raised her children to became the servants of Destined Death and the death of the gods. The Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles thus started their hunts against the gods. Dozens of "gods" would be killed and flayed, and their divine hides were stitched into clothing for their hunters, thus giving them the title of "Godskin" Apostles

The Godskin Apostles wielded twinblade peelers that featured a sickle on one end and a spike for flesh piercing in the other, requiring high skill while the Godskin Nobles, the most ancient apostles, possessed incredible skill with the stitcher swords and wore aprons with seven faces They also stole a power that once represented the gods' wrath, and wielded it as a trophy in the form of a shockwave manifested from their bellies.

At some point during the conflict, some Fire Monks deserted their eternal duty of guardians of the Forge of the Giants and the Giants' Flame contained therein, their long watch having eroded their resolve as they started to succumb to the allure of the Flame's taboo. The first to abandon his post as guardian was Amon, who swore allegiance to the black flames of the gods' hunts and became the first Blackflame Monk. Many more would become traitors of their order, letting themselves be seduced by the black flames of the Gloam Eyed Queen and its apostles.

The God Hunt ended when the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles were defeated by Marika's shadowbound beast, Maliketh.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.markdown:
After the defeat of the Gloam Eyed Queen, Marika's only need for her shadow was to serve as a vessel. On her orders, Maliketh sealed away the Rune of Death, binding it within his Black Blade. Marika's offspring thus obtained a form of immortality owing to the removal of their fated deaths from the Elden Ring, however Maliketh continued to instill fear in the demigods thanks to his blade containing the only power that could still kill them.

As a result of the Rune of Death being sealed, the true power of the black flame of the Godskins was also lost but, despite their Queen's defeat, her surviving Apostles and Nobles continued to remain hidden along with some Blackflame Monks. One Apostle and some Monks managed to flee to the fringes and continued to protect the Godslayer's Greatsword of their Queen deep inside the Divine Tower of Caelid. A Noble and an Apostle would die in the Spiritcaller Cave, still holding onto the swaddling cloth of their Queen.

Following the Shattering, many agents of the Gloam-Eyed Queen would reappear in the Lands Between with the apparent goal of continuing to seek the power of Death or to act against the gods. One Noble would try to infiltrate the Divine Tower of Liurnia where the Cursemark of Death left on Ranni's corpse is found. One Apostle would lead the skinning festivities of Dominula, Windmill Village. One Noble and a Blackflame Monk would protect the Temple of Eiglay, seemingly in serving of the God-Devouring Serpent. A Noble and an Apostle would manage to find their way into Crumbling Farum Azula, where Maliketh continued to protect the Rune of Death sealed inside his flesh.

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.markdown: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, the Hero is the best choice for essentially any build which focuses mainly on Strength. Note that these builds are not necessarily "good", they are just what this origin is better at than any other.

sections.heading: Pure Strength
sections.markdown:
The Hero is by far and away the best origin for a build that increases strength while forsaking all other damage stats, saving 6 entire levels when compared to Wretch. This makes it the best choice for weapons such as the Greatsword or Giant-Crusher, which demand high strength but little of anything else. If a weapon requires 13 or more dexterity to wield, Vagabond will tie with Hero in point efficiency but hero will still outmatch every other origin considerably.

The Hero origin is also either the most efficient or tied for most efficient option for any hybrid class which is focused on raising the strength stat, with the exception of strength/dexterity/intelligence focuses and strength/dexterity/faith focuses, for which prisoner and vagabond are the best options respectively. This makes Hero the best option for essentially any strength hybrid weapon that does not demand high dexterity, such as:

- Ruins Greatsword
- Gargoyle's Black Axe
- Cranial Vessel Candlestand
- Staff of the Avatar
- Troll's Hammer

Note that Astrologer and Prophet both beat out Hero for strength/intelligence and strength/faith builds respectively if the dexterity requirement is 10 or higher, meaning that Hero is not optimal for weapons such as Starscourge Greatsword

sections.heading: Pure Arcane
sections.markdown: Surprisingly, Hero is also the best origin for a build which focuses on ignoring the leveling of other damage stats in favor of only increasing Arcane - although only being 1 level more efficient than both Wretch and Bandit - making it potentially the best option for bleed, poison and occult infusions. However, if the build also requires at least 11 dexterity or 9 intelligence, Bandit then becomes the most optimal origin.

sections.markdown: Heal** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Equipped:**

Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 1,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
The caster kneels in prayer, healing HP equal to 230% of their Faith-based Incantation Scaling, and heals nearby allies for 115% of the same.

 Nearby Revenants and Revenant Followers take damage equal to 50% of their maximum HP plus an additional 300 HP. This attack also breaks their Stance, causing them to become staggered.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 32 FP per cast.
- Costs 35 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- Restores HP equal to 7.19% of Incantation Scaling for each FP spent.
- The healing effect can be delayed indefinitely by holding the casting button, which is helpful if an ally is not yet within range.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- Heal is generally outclassed by the more efficient Great Heal and the significantly stronger Erdtree Heal.
- The healing amount is based on the Faith scaling of an equipped sacred seal. Seals that scale with other attributes will result in reduced healing effectiveness compared to those that focus solely on Faith. 
- This spell breaks the stance of Revenants and Revenant followers, allowing you to quickly cast it again for a potential quick kill. This is the most FP-efficient way to quickly kill Revenants.
 - While technically only the Prophet and Confessor origins have enough Faith to use this incantation by default, it can still be used to kill a Revenant with any starting Origin's base Faith by using the Two Fingers Heirloom (a Prisoner will need another point in Faith, easiest gained with either Marika's Scarseal or a Commoner's Garb or Commoner's Simple Garb).
- All Origins have enough FP to cast this incantation at least 3 times without using a Flask of Cerulean Tears, provided they haven't used FP for anything too expensive.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- This spell is tied with Urgent Heal for the lowest healing effectiveness per FP spent.
- This incantation was included among the starting equipment for the Prophet class during the Closed Network Test.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Greater Potentates** are characters in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Greater Potentates are hostile hornsent with Bonny Butchering Knives. They wear only Caterpillar Masks, which enable them to focus on their ritual. They maimed, killed, and butchered both shamans and their own kind to put them into jars, in hopes that they would be reborn as "saints". They are responsible for the Jar Dwellers.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: The Greater Potentates patrol the Bonny Village, located on the eastern Scadu Altus in the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Greater Potentate respawn when the player rests at a Site of Grace.
- Hornsent (NPC) was a Greater Potentate.
- The Stranded Soul at the Whipping Hut was a Greater Potentate.
- Greater Potentates share a face, which is nearly identical to Hornsent (NPC), who has different facial hair, as well as Madding Hand and Lamenter.
